text: Reset a forgotten password using the recovery email. Existing sessions remain valid until explicitly revoked.
Revoke all active login sessions after a stolen password, then change the credential and enable two factor authentication.
A robot that will not recharge may have dirty charging contacts. Clean the dock contacts with power disconnected.
A robot battery that drains quickly may need replacement. Check battery health and reduce unnecessary idle motion.
Wireless disconnects can be caused by weak signal or router channel interference. Move the access point and inspect signal strength.
A device can show offline even with working wifi when its TLS certificate has expired. Renew the device certificate.
To request a refund for a duplicate payment, provide the two transaction references. Billing support reviews the charge.
Download the monthly invoice from the billing page. An invoice download does not refund a payment.
Delete customer personal data from primary storage and search indexes. Backup copies expire according to the retention schedule.
Restore accidentally deleted documents from a verified backup snapshot. Check that the requested recovery point predates deletion.
A stuck robot wheel can stop motion. Power off the robot and remove the obstruction before a supervised test.
A motor overheating alarm requires stopping the machine and letting it cool. Inspect blocked ventilation before restarting.
An expired TLS certificate causes handshake failures. Renew the certificate and reload the service; do not disable verification.
When disk space is full, rotate old logs according to retention policy. Do not erase the active database.
A forbidden response means the account may lack the required role. Check tenant membership and least privilege permissions.
A login authentication failure can mean an incorrect password. Reset the credential before changing authorization roles.
Use an idempotency key when retrying a payment request after a timeout. A repeated key should return the original result.
A read request timeout can be retried with bounded exponential backoff and jitter. Stop after the retry budget is exhausted.
Back up database snapshots to independent storage and test restore regularly. A successful backup job alone does not prove recovery.
Search results must be filtered by tenant and access permissions before text reaches a reranker or language model.
Error E104 on the sample robot means charging contact failure. Error E140 means motor temperature above the limit.
Error E140 on the sample robot means motor temperature above the limit. Error E104 is unrelated to motor temperature.
Cancel a recurring subscription to stop future invoices. Cancellation does not automatically refund previous payments.
Changing a wireless password disconnects devices that still use the old credential. Update the robot network settings.
Robot charging should pause when the battery is too hot. Let the battery cool and inspect the charger before resuming.
For data export, download a customer archive. Export creates a copy and does not delete the original records.
A storage quota is an account limit, not physical disk failure. Request a quota increase or remove unused files.
Rotate a leaked service API key and revoke the old key. Resetting a user password does not revoke independent service keys.
Search indexes can retain deleted records until a tombstone is applied. Verify deletion in both keyword and vector indexes.
A robot cannot reach its dock when obstacles block the path. Clear the route before inspecting charging electronics.
Use tenant scoped cache keys to prevent one customer receiving another customer search results.
A refund request can time out after being accepted. Reuse the same idempotency key rather than submitting a new refund.
